messages.text: Could you fix these six slides? Five minutes, tops. I need them this afternoon and you're the best at this.
I have my own report due at 4:30. What exactly needs changing, and what did your boss say?

It's really quick — mostly layout stuff, honestly. But okay, since you asked: the boss said the reasoning doesn't hold. Something about how the comparison is argued, not the look. Page three is where the cost argument lives. So can you take all six? Or at least skim them?
I can look at the third page and list questions. I cannot rewrite it or take on the other pages.

Okay, okay — just page three, questions only, got it. But if you're already in there and spot something obvious... you could just fix it, right? And what am I supposed to do with the other five while you're buried in your report? That still leaves me stuck.
I am offering a review, not agreeing to edit anything after 4:30. Does that limited help work for you?

Fine — a review, no edits, I heard you. It's better than nothing. Just... when you list the questions, could you make them concrete? Like 'this number needs a source' rather than 'this feels weak'? That way I can actually work from them myself.

messages.text: If you need all six pages rewritten, you will need another person. I can still list questions for one page if that helps.

It helps, honestly. Questions on page three, I handle the rest — even if that means begging someone else or figuring it out myself. Send me whatever you find whenever you get to it; I'll work around my own deadline from there.

report.summary: You asked what actually needed changing before committing, which exposed a reasoning rewrite rather than quick layout fixes. Your offer — questions on page three only, no edits — stayed consistent through Tang's attempts to expand it, and she accepted it.

alternatives.why: Naming a rough delivery time for even the limited review would give Tang a concrete window to plan around, if you want and can offer one.

knowledge.whyThis: Your line 'I can look at the third page and list questions. I cannot rewrite it' matches 'A Clear No Is a Gift' — a kind no paired with a workable alternative — and the pattern of 'Not Tonight — But 7am Works'.

reflectionQuestions: Tang asked for concrete, actionable questions (like 'this number needs a source') — how will you phrase your page-three notes so she can act on them without further edits from you?
report.nextStep: Next time a 'five-minute favor' lands, ask one scope question before answering, just as you did here.
